articles.title: Department of Labor Scrutinizes PBM Practices Impacting Employer Plans
articles.summary: The Department of Labor is increasing its focus on pharmacy benefit managers and their impact on employer-sponsored health plans. This regulatory attention directly affects self-funded employers by increasing scrutiny on fiduciary responsibilities, PBM pricing transparency, and administrative fees.

articles.title: Drugmakers and PBM Defenders Clash Over Group Purchasing Organizations
articles.summary: Pharmaceutical manufacturers and pharmacy benefit manager defenders are publicly debating the role and influence of group purchasing organizations in the drug supply chain. This conflict highlights ongoing regulatory scrutiny over rebate aggregation and pricing transparency that directly impacts self-funded employer health plans. The outcome of this debate could shift how PBMs negotiate pricing and manage specialty drug costs for employer-sponsored plans.

articles.title: DOL Finalizes PBM Disclosure Rule for Self-Funded Health Plans
articles.summary: The Department of Labor has finalized new disclosure rules requiring PBMs to provide enhanced transparency regarding pricing and compensation to self-funded employer health plans. This regulation directly impacts plan sponsors by enforcing stricter fiduciary oversight over PBM contracts and hidden fees. Self-funded employers must now review their vendor agreements to ensure compliance and evaluate newly uncovered cost streams.
articles.source_line: Source: JD Supra; Mon, 16 Nov 2026 15:58:17 GMT

articles.title: New PBM Final Rule Empowers Self-Funded Employers With Greater Oversight
articles.summary: A newly enacted PBM final rule increases transparency and regulatory oversight, giving self-funded employers more control over their pharmacy benefit plans and contract terms. This development directly impacts how plan sponsors manage drug costs, audits, and PBM relationships.

articles.title: Employer Health Care Cost Projections Exceeded for Self-Funded Plans
articles.summary: Rising medical and pharmacy benefit expenditures are outpacing initial corporate forecasts, putting intense financial pressure on self-funded employers. This escalating cost crunch increases urgency for organizations to adopt aggressive PBM cost-containment strategies, utilization management, and alternative pricing models.

articles.title: Mark Cuban Argues Self-Insured Employers Hold Key to Healthcare Cost Control
articles.summary: Entrepreneur Mark Cuban emphasizes that self-funded employers have the leverage and responsibility to curb soaring U.S. healthcare costs by actively auditing their claims and pharmacy benefit bills. The commentary underscores the critical need for self-funded plan sponsors to demand transparency and scrutinize hidden costs in their benefits administration. This perspective reinforces the value proposition of transparent PBM models that empower employers to control plan spend.
articles.source_line: Source: BigGo Finance; Mon, 16 Nov 2026 19:08:00 GMT

articles.title: Sandoz Launches Eylea Biosimilar Enzeevu in US Market
articles.summary: Sandoz has officially launched Enzeevu, a biosimilar referencing the blockbuster eye drug Eylea, in the United States. This introduction provides self-funded employers and PBMs with a lower-cost alternative for managing high-cost specialty therapy spend within their health plans. Increased biosimilar uptake in the specialty drug category is a key strategy for reducing net plan costs and mitigating specialty inflation.
articles.source_line: Source: The Pharma Letter; Mon, 16 Nov 2026 13:16:20 GMT

articles.title: Wraparound Care Significantly Boosts GLP-1 Weight Loss Outcomes
articles.summary: A new study from Calibrate and Withings shows that combining GLP-1 medications with wraparound lifestyle support increases weight loss by over 60 percent. This finding provides self-funded employers with actionable data to improve plan design, manage high-cost specialty drug spend, and ensure long-term clinical ROI on obesity benefits.
articles.source_line: Source: Fierce Healthcare; Mon, 16 Nov 2026 14:00:00 GMT

articles.title: WTW Predicts Sustained 11% Health Cost Surge for Employers
articles.summary: Willis Towers Watson projects employers will face continued double-digit health benefit cost increases with little near-term relief in sight. This surging cost trend directly impacts self-funded employer health plans, driving the urgency for tighter pharmacy benefit management and cost containment strategies.
articles.source_line: Source: Insurance Business; Mon, 16 Nov 2026 19:19:37 GMT

articles.title: Omada Health Highlights GLP-1 Persistence and AI Tracking Data at ObesityWeek
articles.summary: Omada Health presented new clinical data focusing on 12-month GLP-1 persistence and AI-driven meal tracking tools. For self-funded employers managing surging obesity drug expenditures, understanding medication adherence and digital companion interventions is critical for optimizing benefit ROI.
articles.source_line: Source: Quiver Quantitative; Mon, 16 Nov 2026 14:14:00 GMT

articles.title: CVS Health Study Examines GLP-1 Coverage and Employer Affordability Challenges
articles.summary: A new study from CVS Health analyzes the growing utilization of GLP-1 medications and the escalating financial burden they place on employer-sponsored health plans. The findings highlight the critical tension self-funded employers face in balancing comprehensive obesity benefits with long-term cost sustainability. This analysis directly impacts PBM strategy regarding formulary management and utilization controls for high-cost specialty drugs.
articles.source_line: Source: Chain Drug Review; Mon, 16 Nov 2026 14:24:14 GMT

articles.title: CVS Predicts Financial Break-Even Point for GLP-1 Coverage
articles.summary: CVS Health executives indicate that employer health plans could soon reach a financial break-even point on costly GLP-1 weight-loss drugs as long-term health savings materialize. This analysis directly impacts self-funded employers grappling with how to sustainably manage soaring obesity drug expenditures within their pharmacy benefits.
